1	# Public workspaces: REST routes don't honour the public-read policy
2	
3	**Status:** unfixed, not started. Handoff for a fresh agent.
4	**Repro host:** https://legal-review.lobu.ai (org `legal-review`, visibility `public`)
5	**Written:** 2026-07-30, against `origin/main` @ `e8b09ad9`
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Symptom
10	
11	On a **public** workspace, some pages render for a non-member and others fail:
12	
13	| URL | result |
14	|---|---|
15	| `legal-review.lobu.ai/activity` | ✅ renders |
16	| `legal-review.lobu.ai/connectors` | ✅ renders |
17	| `legal-review.lobu.ai/` (org root) | ❌ "Couldn't load the workspace builder. / You are not a member of this organization" |
18	| sidebar agents list | ❌ empty |
19	
20	The error text is the **server's raw authz sentence** printed as product copy (see "Related, already fixed" below — the same render path).
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Root cause
25	
26	The public-read carve-out can only evaluate **tool calls**, never REST routes.
27	
28	`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:180` — `canAccessPublicOrgRequest()`:
29	
30	```js
31	if (!requestedToolName) return false;                              // REST routes have no toolName param
32	if (isMcpRoute) return false;
33	if (!['POST','PUT','PATCH'].includes(c.req.method.toUpperCase())) return false;  // a GET can never qualify
34	```
35	
36	Consumed at `multi-tenant.ts:200`:
37	```js
38	const allowOrgLevelPublicRead =
39	  requestedOrgVisibility === 'public' && (await canAccessPublicOrgRequest());
40	```
41	
42	When it returns false the request never reaches its handler — the middleware answers with
43	`multi-tenant.ts:610` (anonymous → 401 `Authentication required. Use OAuth or API key.`) or
44	`multi-tenant.ts:566` (authenticated non-member → 403 `You are not a member of this organization`).
45	
46	So: pages that read through `POST /api/{org}/{tool}` work; pages that read through
47	`GET /api/{org}/...` REST routes do not.
48	
49	- Activity → `resolve_path`, `manage_operations.list_activity|list_runs` (allow-listed) ✅
50	- Connectors → `manage_connections.list`, `manage_catalog.list_catalog`, `/api/{org}/public/connectors` ✅
51	- Agents list → `GET /api/{org}/agents` ❌
52	- Org root → `GET /api/{org}/agents/system-agent` ❌
53	
54	---
55	
56	## The actual bug: same data, two doors, opposite answers
57	
58	`packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:181` — the policy **already says agent reads are public**:
59	
60	```js
61	// `list`/`get` are org-read-gated in the handler (requireOrgReadAccess);
62	// the mutating siblings stay owner-admin (OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS).
63	manage_agents: new Set(["list", "get"]),   // inside PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS (declared at :148)
64	```
65	
66	Verified live, anonymous, no credentials:
67	
68	```
69	$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/agents
70	401
71	
72	$ curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"action":"list"}' \
73	    https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/manage_agents
74	{"action":"list","agents":[]}          # 200
75	```
76	
77	**This is a transport gap, not a policy gap.** The intended policy is written down and
78	enforced on one door; the REST door never consults it.
79	
80	Full anonymous probe set:
81	```
82	/api/legal-review/resolve_path          GET 200  POST 200
83	/api/legal-review/public/connectors     GET 200
84	/api/legal-review/manage_agents         POST {"action":"list"} 200
85	/api/legal-review/agents                GET 401
86	/api/legal-review/agents/system-agent   GET 401
87	```
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Two sub-problems — fix them separately
92	
93	### 1. REST routes ignore `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` (server) — a real defect
94	
95	Agent list/get is *supposed* to be publicly readable. Two directions:
96	
97	- **(a) class fix:** teach the REST layer the same policy, so every `/api/{org}/*` REST route
98	  that has a public-readable tool equivalent behaves consistently.
99	  Matches AGENTS.md "fix the class, not the instance". **Do the enumeration first** — count how
100	  many REST routes are in this position before committing to the shape.
101	- **(b) instance fix:** point the SPA's agent reads at the tool transport.
102	  Smaller, no server change, but leaves the next REST route to rediscover this.
103	
104	Recommend starting with the enumeration, then choosing. Do not assume (a) is small.
105	
106	### 2. The org root asks for the builder regardless of viewer (frontend) — a product call
107	
108	`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner.tsx:42` calls `useSystemAgentId()` unconditionally, and
109	`:110-117` renders `systemAgentError.message` verbatim.
110	
111	No policy change can make this one work: **the workspace builder is genuinely owner-only** —
112	there is no public "system agent" concept, and `set_system_agent` is in `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS`.
113	The root must stop requesting it for non-members and render the public workspace view instead.
114	
115	Pieces that already exist and should be reused rather than rebuilt:
116	- `useCurrentOrg()` → `{ org, isMember, isPublic, isLoading }`
117	- `PublicOrgJoinBar` — already mounted in `components/shell/responsive-app-shell.tsx` for exactly this audience
118	- SSR already injects `window.__LOBU_PUBLIC_BOOTSTRAP__` with `resolvedPath.workspace` for public orgs
119	  (confirmed present on legal-review)
120	- `resolve_path` already serves the workspace root anonymously
121	
122	**Open design question for the user:** what exactly a non-member sees at a public workspace root.
123	Leading proposal: the public workspace view + join CTA for non-members; builder unchanged for members.
124	Do not implement past this without confirming.
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Related, already fixed — do NOT redo
129	
130	lobu **#2358** (`e8b09ad9`) / owletto **#646** (`c4661c7a`), merged 2026-07-30.
131	
132	Added `packages/owletto/src/lib/sign-in-redirect.ts` (`signInSearch`, `currentCallbackUrl`,
133	`useAnonymousSignInRedirect`), consolidated 3 duplicate guards + 7 copies of the 7-key
134	`/auth/login` search literal, and applied the guard at the `$owner` layout.
135	
136	That covers **anonymous + private org → redirect to sign-in**. It deliberately does *not* fire here:
137	- the public-bootstrap check suppresses the redirect (correct — a public org must render signed-out)
138	- for an authenticated non-member `!session` is false
139	
140	So the three viewer states at the org root are:
141	
142	| viewer | org | state |
143	|---|---|---|
144	| anonymous | private | ✅ fixed in #2358 |
145	| authenticated non-member | private | ❌ raw 403 |
146	| any non-member | **public** | ❌ this document |
147	
148	An **outage** (5xx) must keep rendering the error rather than bouncing to sign-in — that
149	distinction is deliberate and covered by a test in `owner-root-redirect.test.tsx`. Preserve it.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Separate follow-up, also unfixed
154	
155	`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts` — the session block ends in a bare `catch {}`
156	that silently reinterprets **any** session-validation failure as "anonymous", with no log line.
157	~87 production 401s produced zero signal in the pod logs because of it. Needs at minimum a
158	`logger.warn`. Arguably violates the AGENTS.md "fail closed with a visible log" invariant.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Repro
163	
164	```bash
165	# public org, no credentials
166	curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/agents          # 401
167	curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"action":"list"}' \
168	  https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/manage_agents                                          # 200
169	
170	# confirm the org really is public
171	kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
172	  psql -U postgres -d owletto -t -A -c \
173	  "SELECT slug, visibility FROM organization WHERE slug='legal-review';"                               # legal-review|public
174	```
175	
176	Local: `make task-setup NAME=<slug>`, then the boot recipe. Note the local dev org
177	(`local-install`) is **private** and single-user mode auto-signs-in via `POST /api/local-init`
178	— to exercise the anonymous/non-member path you must stub `authConfig.singleUserMode=false`
179	and refuse `/api/local-init`, or the SPA silently authenticates you.

You're right, and the codebase already agrees with you on two of its three doors. Here's what the evidence shows.

**`/public/*` earns nothing.** `publicRestGetBehaviors` and `restGetBehaviors` call the *same* tool with the *same* params. The only difference is how the context is built — `publicToolContext(url, orgId)` vs `toToolContext(extractAuthContext(c))`. Same projection, same fields, no anonymous-specific narrowing. It's transport duplication, not a security boundary.

**`isPublicReadable` is already the single allow-list — three call sites:**

| door | anonymous on a public org | gated where |
|---|---|---|
| MCP | let in wholesale (`multi-tenant.ts:203`) | per tool call, `mcp-handler.ts:1092` |
| tool transport | gated in middleware (`:194`) | *again* at `tools/execute.ts:184` |
| REST | **blocked** | nowhere — no gate exists |

So MCP already does exactly what you're describing: open the door for a public org, then check each read against `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` at execution time.

**Why REST can't simply be opened the same way:** its handlers have no execution-time gate at all. `agent-routes.ts:369` reads `c.get("organizationId")` and trusts it — membership is enforced *only* by `mcpAuth` in the middleware. And the handler-level check that does exist is not a boundary: `canReadOrg` is `if (!ctx.userId) return true` — anonymous passes. Open the middleware for public orgs and `GET /notifications`, `/deployments`, `/clients`, `/write-permissions` and every `PUT`/`DELETE` open with it.

So the missing capability is the gate, not a URL. Give the REST door the same execution-time check the other two doors already have, against the same list — then `/public/*` has no reason to exist and comes out.

**What that means concretely:**
- REST routes declare the `(tool, action)` they're the REST face of, at their registration site — `agents` → `manage_agents.list`, `agents/:id` → `.get`, and the same for `connections`, `runs`, `actions/available`, `installed`. Not a path text-match; a declaration next to the handler.

- Delete `/api/{org}/public/*` and the SPA's parallel hooks (`usePublicConnectorDefinitions`, the `/public/knowledge/search` and `/public/classifiers` fetches, plus their MSW handlers).

input.content:
# Design: consolidate public-read enforcement onto one allow-list

**Repo:** lobu (`~/Code/lobu`), against `origin/main` @ `e8b09ad9`
**Status:** DESIGN — not implemented. Reviewing before writing code.

---

## 1. Problem

On a **public** workspace, the same data answers differently depending on which
transport asks for it. Verified anonymously against prod (`atlas`, public org, 2 agents):

```
POST /api/atlas/manage_agents  {"action":"list"}   -> 200, returns both agents
GET  /api/atlas/agents                             -> 401
GET  /api/atlas/agents/system-agent                -> 401
```

The policy already says agent reads are public — `packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:181`,
inside `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`:

```ts
manage_agents: new Set(["list", "get"]),
```

So this is a transport gap, not a policy gap. One door enforces the policy; another
door never consults it.

Full anonymous probe of org-scoped REST on prod — every `mcpAuth`-guarded route is 401,
every `/public/*` route is 200:

| `GET /api/{org}/…` | anon | public-readable tool equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| `agents`, `agents/:id` | 401 | `manage_agents.list` / `.get` ✅ |
| `connections`, `connections/:id` | 401 | `manage_connections.list` / `.get` ✅ |
| `runs` | 401 | `manage_operations.list_runs` ✅ |
| `actions/available` | 401 | `manage_operations.list_available` ✅ |
| `installed` | 401 | `manage_catalog.list_installed` ✅ |
| `behaviors` | 401 | `manage_behaviors.list` ✅ — already duplicated to `/public/behaviors` |
| `knowledge/search` | 401 | ✅ — already duplicated to `/public/knowledge/search` |
| `agents/system-agent` | 401 | **none** — stays closed, see §6 |
| `notifications`, `deployments`, `clients`, `tools` | 401 | none — correctly closed |

---

## 2. Architecture finding

`isPublicReadable(toolName, args)` (`auth/tool-access.ts:307`) is already the single
allow-list. It has three call sites, and the three doors are gated inconsistently:

| door | anonymous on a public org | gated where |
|---|---|---|
| MCP | admitted wholesale — `multi-tenant.ts:203` `allowAnonymousPublicOrgMcp` | per tool call, `mcp-handler.ts:1092` |
| tool transport (`POST /api/{org}/{toolName}`) | admitted by `multi-tenant.ts:194` after sniffing the JSON body | **again** at `tools/execute.ts:184` |
| REST (`GET /api/{org}/…`) | never admitted | **nowhere — no gate exists** |

MCP already implements the model we want: open the door for a public org, then check
each read against the allow-list at execution time.

**REST cannot simply be opened the same way**, because REST handlers have no
execution-time gate:

- `lobu/agent-routes.ts:369` (`GET /agents`) reads `c.get("organizationId")` and trusts it.
  No membership check of its own.
- The handler-level check that does exist is not a boundary. `canReadOrg`
  (`utils/organization-access.ts:140`) is:
  ```ts
  if (!ctx.organizationId) return false;
  if (!ctx.userId) return true;      // <-- anonymous PASSES
  ```
  So `requireOrgReadAccess` cannot hold a door shut against anonymous.

Membership for REST is enforced **only** by `mcpAuth` in the middleware, at two points —
`multi-tenant.ts:562` (authenticated non-member → 403) and `:606` (anonymous → 401).
Both already read `allowOrgLevelPublicRead || allowAnonymousPublicOrgMcp`.

Consequence: if the middleware were opened for public orgs without a per-route gate,
`GET /notifications`, `/deployments`, `/clients`, `/write-permissions` and every
`PUT`/`DELETE` would open with it. **Some enumeration is mandatory.**

## 2b. `/api/{org}/public/*` is redundant, not a boundary

The public namespace is transport duplication, not a narrower projection.
`publicRestGetBehaviors` (`rest-api.ts:198`) and `restGetBehaviors` (`:~140`) call the
**same** tool with the **same** params. The only difference is context construction:

```ts
// public:  publicToolContext(c.req.url, organizationId)   // userId:null, memberRole:null,
//                                                          // isAuthenticated:false, SCOPE_CHECK_NOT_APPLICABLE
// member:  toToolContext(extractAuthContext(c))
```

Same fields returned either way. So `/public/*` is a **second enumeration** of what is
publicly readable, parallel to and independently maintained from `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`.
Two lists that must agree and have no mechanism forcing them to.

---

## 3. Proposal

**One allow-list, consulted by all three doors.** Give the REST door the same
execution-time gate MCP and the tool transport already have, then delete the
`/public/*` namespace as redundant.

1. REST routes **declare** the `(tool, action)` they are the REST face of, at their
   registration site.
2. `mcpAuth` admits anonymous / non-member callers on a **public** org only when the
   matched route carries such a declaration **and** `isPublicReadable(tool, action)`
   returns true — the same predicate the other two doors use.
3. Admitted callers get an anonymous context (`memberRole: null`, `mcpIsAuthenticated:
   false`), identical in shape to what `publicToolContext` builds today.
4. `/api/{org}/public/*` routes and their SPA hooks are deleted.

Default stays **closed**: a route with no declaration behaves exactly as today.

### Declaration surface (7 routes)

| method + path | declares |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/agents` | `manage_agents` / `list` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/agents/:agentId` | `manage_agents` / `get` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/connections` | `manage_connections` / `list` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/connections/:id` | `manage_connections` / `get` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/runs` | `manage_operations` / `list_runs` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/actions/available` | `manage_operations` / `list_available` |
| `GET /api/:orgSlug/installed` | `manage_catalog` / `list_installed` |

### Deletions

Server (`index.ts` registrations + `rest-api.ts` handlers):
`/public/knowledge/search`, `/public/classifiers`, `/public/connectors`,
`/public/connectors/:connectorKey`, `/public/organization`, `/public/events`,
`/public/behaviors` — plus `withPublicOrg`, `publicToolContext`,
`resolvePublicOrganizationId` once unreferenced.

Frontend (`packages/owletto`, submodule — separate PR, merged first):
`usePublicConnectorDefinitions` (`lib/api/connections.ts:374`), the
`/public/knowledge/search` fetch (`lib/api/content.ts:148`), the `/public/classifiers`
fetch (`:266`), and the MSW handlers in `test/handlers.ts:80-85`.

---

## 4. The hard part — where the declaration lives (REVIEW THIS)

The declaration must be readable by `mcpAuth` **before** it decides. Hono runs
middleware in registration order, so a per-route middleware registered *after*
`mcpAuth` is too late.

This is straightforward for routes registered directly on `app` in `index.ts`
(`connections`, `runs`, `actions/available`) — insert a declaring middleware ahead of
`mcpAuth` at the registration site.

It is **not** straightforward for `agentRoutes` and `orgInstalledRoutes`, which are
mounted sub-routers that apply `mcpAuth` router-wide:

```ts
// lobu/agent-routes.ts:164
routes.use("*", mcpAuth);
routes.use("*", async (c, next) => {
  const orgId = c.get("organizationId");
  if (!orgId) return c.json({ error: "Organization required" }, 401);
  return orgContext.run({ organizationId: orgId }, next);
});
```

A per-route declaration inside that router runs after `mcpAuth`. Options:

- **(i) Registration helper.** A wrapper that both registers the route and records
  `(method, routePath) -> {tool, action}` in a registry `mcpAuth` consults via
  `c.req.routePath`. Single source of truth for the pattern string; not a hand-written
  URL matcher. **Unverified:** what `c.req.routePath` returns inside a sub-router
  mounted with `app.route('/api/:orgSlug/agents', routes)` — relative or absolute?
  If relative, the registry key needs the mount prefix, which reintroduces a string
  the helper does not own.
- **(ii) Declare at the router level, before `mcpAuth`.** e.g. a
  `routes.use("*", declareIfMatches({...}))` ahead of `routes.use("*", mcpAuth)`.
  Rejected: matching sub-paths inside that middleware is a URL text-matcher deciding
  authz, which is the shape we are trying to avoid.
- **(iii) Split the sub-routers** so public-readable routes register on `app` directly
  with an explicit chain. Most explicit, largest diff, and fights the refactor at
  `agent-routes.ts:156-170` that deliberately hoisted `mcpAuth` to the router.

Leaning (i). **Want a review verdict on this specifically**, plus whether the
`c.req.routePath` behaviour makes it viable.

---

## 5. Data exposure — must be settled before widening

`manage_agents.list` returns `owner_user_id` to anonymous callers **today** through the
tool door. Verified on prod, no credentials:

```json
{"id":"atlas-curator","owner_platform":"lobu",
 "owner_user_id":"8a2D2Yb57odFHO2PldhD6n392Cf6456B", ...}
```

Pre-existing on an already-open door, but this change widens the audience. Intent is to

The documented helper explicitly shows this usage: [index.d.ts:39](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/node_modules/hono/dist/types/helper/route/index.d.ts:39). `baseRoutePath(c, -1)` also returned the mounted `/api/:orgSlug/agents` prefix, allowing a router-local registry to derive the relative pattern without hard-coding the mount.
122	
123	Verdicts:
124	
125	- **(i): revise and use.** Do not use `c.req.routePath`; use Hono’s matched-route helper with `-1`, plus a router-scoped immutable registry. Registry miss or ambiguity must deny.
126	- **(ii): reject.** A hand-written raw-URL matcher is unnecessary and brittle.
127	- **(iii): fallback only.** Structurally safest, but the official Hono final-match helper avoids the large split.
128	
129	Add an integration test against a mounted router, including static/dynamic collisions such as `/agents/system-agent` and `/installed/agents/:agentId/installed`.
130	
131	A deterministic immutable registry created at boot is replica-local configuration, not shared mutable state, so it does not violate the multi-replica invariant.
132	
133	---
134	
135	### P1 — `(tool, action)` is the wrong general authorization capability
136	
137	It works only when the REST handler literally executes that tool with a server-fixed action and returns its output. That is true for connections, runs and available actions. It is false for agents and installed catalog.
138	
139	Coupling a richer REST representation to `manage_agents.list` means any future REST-only field is silently public merely because the tool action remains allowed. Conversely, renaming or splitting a tool can accidentally close an unrelated stable REST API.
140	
141	Recommendation: authorize stable data capabilities/projections, for example:
142	
143	- `agents.public-summary.list`
144	- `connections.public-summary.read`
145	- `operations.public-catalog.list`
146	
147	Map tools and REST routes to the same capability only when they use the same canonical serializer. Keep tool/action checks as execution authorization for actual tool calls. A route declaration should not confer public access to an arbitrary handler merely because a roughly analogous tool exists.
148	
149	---
150	
151	### P1 — the test plan would miss the most dangerous regressions
152	
153	Add:
154	
155	1. **Projection contract tests:** compare allowed REST and tool outputs or assert an exact public key allow-list. Explicitly forbid agent settings/prompts, owner IDs, connect tokens, auth-profile identifiers, server file paths, run inputs/outputs/checkpoints and creator IDs.
156	2. **Full auth matrix:** anonymous, session non-member, OAuth non-member, PAT non-member, member and admin against public/private orgs.
157	3. **Tenant-collision fixtures:** same agent ID and connection-like identifiers in two orgs; prove counts and returned rows remain isolated.
158	4. **Argument-substitution tests:** `?action=delete`, duplicate `action` parameters and malformed/coerced query values.
159	5. **Routing-collision tests:** `/agents/system-agent`, inference-provider literals, `/installed/agents/:agentId/installed`, unknown paths, trailing slash, HEAD and OPTIONS.
160	6. **Default-close inventory test:** register a new route under each router and prove it is closed without a declaration. Generate the inventory from actual Hono routes rather than maintaining another handwritten list.
161	7. **Visibility-transition test:** public → private while org visibility is cached; the next request must close.
162	8. **Failure tests:** DB/cache/registry errors must deny, never fall through as public.
163	9. **SSE tests:** public subscribers receive only the four approved invalidation keys; member streams retain full behavior; ticket and cookie authentication still work.
164	10. **Namespace migration tests:** parameter and response parity for each replaced `/public/*` endpoint, plus a staged compatibility decision. “Every deletion has a declared equivalent” is insufficient and currently false.
165	
166	## Final decision
167	
168	The design should be reconsidered at its core authorization abstraction before implementation.
169	
170	Required revisions:
171	
172	1. Remove agent routes and `/installed` from the seven claimed equivalents.
173	2. Audit and create explicit public DTOs for connections and runs; eliminate connect-token and run-payload exposure.
174	3. Replace generic `(tool, action)` coupling with projection-level capabilities, except for routes that literally proxy a fixed tool action.
175	4. Use Hono’s `routePath(c, -1)`/`baseRoutePath` seam with fail-closed registry tests.
176	5. Specify public-viewer identity semantics across session, PAT and OAuth callers.
177	6. Treat `/public/*` removal as a separate compatibility migration; keep filtered SSE separate.
178	7. Expand the tests above before widening any route.
179	
180	No files were modified; the workspace remained clean.

content.text: Let me verify one more live claim — codex says the REST wrappers let `?action=` override the server-fixed action.
Confirmed — query spread lands **after** the fixed action, so `?action=` overrides it. Let me check whether anything downstream stops that.

Review is back, and I verified its main claims against source and prod rather than taking them on trust. Two of my own design claims were wrong.

**Codex verdict: reconsider the core authorization abstraction before implementing.** I agree — the design as written would have widened exposure past what the allow-list actually authorizes.

## What I got wrong

**`/public/*` is not redundant.** I checked `behaviors`, found it was a thin wrapper, and asserted the whole namespace was. It isn't. `/public/knowledge/search` accepts *more* params than its authed sibling (`rest-api.ts:442` vs `:395` — optional query, engagement bounds, classification filters); `/public/connectors/:key` is a unique composite projection with no equivalent anywhere; `/public/organization` has no public-readable tool at all; `/public/events` applies a strict invalidation-key filter that `/events` doesn't. The "every deletion has a declared equivalent" test I proposed could not have passed honestly.

**"REST handlers have no execution-time gate" is false for 4 of 7.** `connections`, `runs`, `actions/available` go through `restToolProxy` → `executeTool` → `isPublicReadable` (`execute.ts:184`). Only the two agent routes and `/installed` lack it.

## The finding that kills the design as written

`PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` is an *action-name* allow-list. It says nothing about fields. `manage_connections.list` is `SELECT c.*` (`crud.ts:270`) plus a live-token subselect (`:305`).

Verified anonymously against prod, no credentials, `market.lobu.ai` (public org, 11 org-visible connections):

```
total: 2   field count: 49
connect_token present: True  = None
created_by = '8a2D2Yb57odFHO2PldhD6n392Cf6456B'
created_by_username = 'buremba'
```

`config` and `credentials` come back null on these rows, and there are **0 pending connect tokens org-wide right now**, so nothing is actively leaking a credential. But `connect_token` is wired into the anonymous response shape — any connect flow started on an org-visible connection in a public org would expose a live 1-hour bearer capability to unauthenticated callers. Blast radius today is one org, whose connections you created. Latent, not burning.

So declaring `GET /connections` "equivalent to `manage_connections.list`" would have inherited all 49 fields. Same story for `list_runs` (returns run input/output/checkpoints, `manage_operations.ts:1487`) and `/installed` (`source_uri` can be a server-local `file://` path).

## Separate issue I hit while verifying

The REST wrappers build args as `{ action: "list", ...c.req.query() }` (`index.ts:1232`, `:1256`, `:1264`) — spread lands *after*, so `?action=delete` overrides the server-fixed action, and `restToolProxy` passes it straight to `executeTool` unmodified. Anonymous callers are stopped by the access-level check, but a **member** is not: `GET /api/{org}/connections?action=delete&connection_id=N` would perform the delete. Whether that's remotely triggerable depends on the session cookie's SameSite setting, which I haven't checked. Unrelated to public orgs — affects every org.

## Useful result

Codex empirically resolved §4: `c.req.routePath` returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents/*` before `next()` (can't distinguish list from detail), but Hono's `routePath(c, -1)` returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents` and `/api/:orgSlug/agents/:agentId` correctly. So the registration-helper seam works — just not via the property I assumed.

12	- **Node 22 required** — `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin` (active shell may be node 26, which the repo rejects). Prefix `PATH`.
13	- **Build `@lobu/pgvector-embedded` first** (`cd packages/pgvector-embedded && bun run build`) or vitest dies with `ERR_RESOLVE_PACKAGE_ENTRY_FAIL` (the global-setup imports it). Other workspace deps too → `make build-packages` (also builds the owletto SPA, validating UI changes compile).
14	- **DB backend:** global-setup uses `DATABASE_URL` if set, else spawns **ephemeral embedded PG18+pgvector** (same engine as `lobu run`). `make review` *unsets* DATABASE_URL to force embedded.
15	- **macOS embedded-PG shm gotcha:** embedded PG fails with `could not create shared memory segment: No space left on device` once the kernel `SHMMNI` cap (~32) is hit by leaked 56-byte Postgres interlock segments from prior runs. Fix: remove detached ones — `for id in $(ipcs -mob | awk '$1=="m" && $5=="<user>" && $7==0 {print $2}'); do ipcrm -m "$id"; done` (only `nattch=0`; never touch the running Homebrew PG's attached segment).
16	- **Alt to embedded:** `createdb watcher_exec_test` on Homebrew PG17 (has pgvector 0.8.1) + `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5432/watcher_exec_test?sslmode=disable LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1` (test-db.ts wipes/migrates; name must contain "test").
17	- **`make dev` (the dev SERVER, ≠ the vitest harness) needs a PRE-MIGRATED external DATABASE_URL.** It only schema-version-*checks* at boot (`schema-version-check.ts`); it does NOT apply migrations. An empty/fresh DB → it boots ("Lobu running at …") then exits with `relation "public.schema_migrations" does not exist`. /**
 * Argument composition for fixed-action REST routes.
 *
 * Lives apart from `rest-api.ts` so it can be unit-tested without importing
 * the tool registry (importing `rest-api` pulls the whole tool graph).
 */

/**
 * Compose tool args for a REST route whose action the SERVER picks: caller
 * params first, the server's action last so it always wins.
 *
 * Routes used to build these as `{ action: 'list', ...c.req.query() }` — the
 * caller's params spread last, so `?action=delete` replaced the route's own
 * action. `executeTool` still refused callers without the required access
 * level, so this was not privilege escalation; it was a write reachable by
 * GET. The session cookie is SameSite=Lax, which is sent on top-level
 * cross-site GET navigations, so a plain link could make an already-authorized
 * member or admin perform the write.
 */
export function fixedActionArgs(
	action: string,
	callerArgs?: Record<string, unknown>
): Record<string, unknown> {
	return { ...callerArgs, action };
}

Still green. The build is running; I'll run the full gates when it lands. Here's where things stand.

## Fix 1 built: `?action=` override (CSRF-shaped)

Red → green evidence, both captured:

```
RED  (composition reverted):  Expected: "list"  Received: "delete"   → 4 pass, 2 fail
GREEN (fix restored):                                                → 6 pass, 0 fail
```

I also mutation-tested the coverage guard — regressing one call site back to the old shape makes it fail (`Expected length: 1, Received length: 2`), so the guard actually asserts its coverage rather than passing vacuously.

Diff (`git diff --stat`): `index.ts` +13/−18, `rest-api.ts` +26, plus two new files.

The fix is at the chokepoint rather than per-site — `restToolAction(c, tool, action, callerArgs)` applies the action **last**, so no call site can get the order wrong. All 7 fixed-action wrappers now route through it; the one remaining bare `restToolProxy(c)` is the generic `POST /api/:orgSlug/:toolName` passthrough, where a caller-supplied action is the design and `executeTool` authorizes per call.

**Severity, stated accurately:** this is *not* privilege escalation — `executeTool` re-checks access level, so an anonymous caller could never delete anything. It's that a write became reachable by GET, and with `SameSite=Lax` a cross-site link carries the session cookie on a top-level navigation. So a link could make an already-authorized user perform a write they didn't intend. The sharpest case is `GET /api/{org}/runs?action=approve&run_id=N` — member-tier, and it hands over exactly the human decision the approval gate exists to require.

## Still owed on this branch

`make pre-pr` and the full unit suite once the build finishes, then commit → PR. I have not run those yet, so I'm not claiming this is verified beyond the focused test.

## Not started

**Fix 2 (`connect_token` field exposure)** — separate branch, as I proposed. Narrower than it first looked: 0 pending tokens exist org-wide right now, and only one public org (`market`) has org-visible connections, so nothing is currently leaking. What *is* live is `created_by` / `created_by_username` on those 11 rows.

**The consolidation itself** — design needs the revisions codex listed before it's worth implementing. Two of my original claims were wrong (`/public/*` isn't redundant; 4 of 7 routes do have an execution-time gate), so §2b and §3 need rewriting, and the `(tool, action)` coupling probably needs to become projection-level capabilities for the two agent routes and `/installed`.

Both questions I asked earlier are still open and still worth your call — particularly the abstraction one, since it decides whether the consolidation is a contained change or a new capability vocabulary across both doors.

Both suites green (745 + 64 pass, 0 fail). pre-pr re-running. Current state:

## Two fixes on the branch, one root cause

A caller-supplied `action` key overriding a server-fixed one. Found in REST, then grep-enumerated per the class rule and found again in the SDK sandbox.

**1. REST fixed-action routes** (`index.ts`, `rest-api.ts`, new `http/rest-tool-action.ts`)
`{ action: "list", ...c.req.query() }` → caller params spread last. All 7 wrappers now go through `restToolAction`, which applies the action last.

```
RED:   Expected: "list"  Received: "delete"    → 4 pass, 2 fail
GREEN:                                          → 6 pass, 0 fail
```

**2. SDK `entitySchema` namespace** (`sandbox/namespaces/entity-schema.ts`)
This one is the more interesting find. `action-call.ts:188` already strips a caller `action` and documents exactly why — but `callEntity` handed it `payload.action as string`, read off the *already-merged* payload. So the strip protected the input while the caller still chose the handler:

```
entitySchema.listTypes({ action: 'delete', slug: 'x' })
  → callEntity({action:'delete', ...}) → action('delete', …) → delete
```

The manifest had only admitted a read method. `executeTool` still re-checks caller tier, so a low-tier caller gains nothing — but it defeats `query_sdk` read-mode for an admin caller, which is the whole point of read-mode.

```
RED  (guard vs `git show HEAD:…entity-schema.ts`):  offenders == ["entity-schema.ts"]  → 1 fail
GREEN (fixed):                                                                          → 2 pass
```

Both guards are mutation-tested — regressing a REST call site trips the registration guard (`Expected length: 1, Received length: 2`), and the namespace guard fires on the real pre-fix file, not a synthetic one.

## Accuracy note on severity

Neither is privilege escalation — `executeTool` re-checks access level in both paths. What each does is let an *already-authorized* principal be steered into a write they didn't request: by cross-site link for REST (`SameSite=Lax` carries the cookie on top-level GET), and by a read-mode script for the sandbox. ## Summary

- A caller-supplied `action` key could override the action a server-side call site had fixed, in two places. Neither is privilege escalation — `executeTool` re-checks the caller's access level on both paths — but each lets an **already-authorized** principal be steered into a write they did not request.
- **REST**: fixed-action routes built args as `{ action: "list", ...c.req.query() }`, spreading caller params *last*. `GET /api/{org}/runs?action=approve&run_id=N` reached `manage_operations` as an approve. The session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, which is sent on top-level cross-site GET navigations, so a plain link was enough. Fixed at the chokepoint: all 7 wrappers now go through `restToolAction`, which applies the action last.
- **SDK sandbox**: `action-call.ts` already strips a caller `action` for exactly this reason, but `entity-schema.ts`'s `callEntity`/`callRel` passed it `payload.action as string` — read back off the already-merged payload. `entitySchema.listTypes({ action: 'delete' })` dispatched a delete while the SDK manifest had only admitted a read method, defeating `query_sdk` read-mode for an admin caller. `actionName` is now a literal from each call site.

Found the REST instance first; the sandbox one came from grep-enumerating the class per AGENTS.md rather than from a second review round.

## Corrections from the 2026-07-30 design review (codex + prod probes) — the original handoff doc was wrong on three points

1. **`legal-review` has 0 agent rows.** Its empty sidebar is truthful data, NOT the 401. Do not use it as the witness. Use **`atlas`** (public, 2 agents incl. a system agent): there `manage_agents.list` returns both agents anonymously while `GET /api/atlas/agents` is 401. Public orgs w/ agents: atlas 2, devops/market/delivery 1 each.
2. **`/api/{org}/public/*` is NOT redundant** — do not plan to delete it. Only `behaviors` is a thin wrapper. `/public/knowledge/search` accepts MORE params than its authed sibling (`rest-api.ts:442` vs `:395`); `/public/connectors/:key` is a unique composite projection with no equivalent; `/public/organization` has no public-readable tool at all; `/public/events` applies a strict invalidation-key filter `/events` lacks. Checking one handler and generalizing to the namespace was the error.
3. **"REST has no execution-time gate" is false for 4 of 7 routes.** `connections`, `runs`, `actions/available` go through `restToolProxy` → `executeTool` → `isPublicReadable` (`tools/execute.ts:184`). Only the two agent routes and `/installed` lack it.

**The finding that reshapes the design:** `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` is an *action-name* allow-list and says nothing about FIELDS. `manage_connections.list` is `SELECT c.*` (`crud.ts:270`) + a live `connect_token` subselect (`:305`). Verified anonymous on prod `market.lobu.ai`: **49 fields**, incl. `created_by`, `created_by_username`, and `connect_token` (null only because 0 tokens pending). `list_runs` returns run input/output/checkpoints; `/installed` leaks `source_uri` (can be a server-local `file://`). So "declare REST route ≡ tool action" would inherit every field — the declaration must gate the PROJECTION, not just the route.

**Design verdict:** implement projection-level capabilities with one canonical serializer per capability, or keep `(tool, action)` coupling ONLY for routes that literally proxy a fixed tool action (connections/runs/actions — which already gate at `executeTool`), and give agents + `/installed` explicit public DTOs.

**Hono seam (empirically resolved):** `c.req.routePath` returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents/*` before `next()` — useless for distinguishing list from detail. Use Hono's `routePath(c, -1)` helper, which returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents` and `/api/:orgSlug/agents/:agentId` correctly; `baseRoutePath(c, -1)` gives the mount prefix. Registry miss must deny.

**The class:** a call site fixes a tool `action`, then spreads caller-controlled data *after* it, so the caller picks the handler.

1. **REST** — `index.ts` wrappers built `{ action: "list", ...c.req.query() }`. 5 of 7 sites affected. `GET /api/{org}/runs?action=approve&run_id=N` reached `manage_operations` as an approve; `?action=delete` on connections likewise. Session cookie is **SameSite=Lax** (`auth/routes.ts:334`), sent on top-level cross-site GET navigations → a plain link was enough.
2. **SDK sandbox** — `action-call.ts:188` ALREADY strips a caller `action` and documents why, but `entity-schema.ts` `callEntity`/`callRel` passed it `payload.action as string`, read off the already-merged payload. `entitySchema.listTypes({action:'delete'})` dispatched a delete while the manifest had only admitted a read method → defeats `query_sdk` read-mode for an admin caller.

**Severity, precisely:** NOT privilege escalation. `executeTool` (`tools/execute.ts:184`) re-checks the caller's access level on both paths, so a low-tier caller gains nothing. What it does is let an *already-authorized* principal be steered into a write they didn't request.

**Fix shape:** chokepoint, not per-site. `restToolAction(c, tool, action, callerArgs)` in `rest-api.ts` applies the action LAST; every fixed-action route goes through it. In the sandbox, `actionName` must be a literal from the call site, never read back off a payload.

**Type trap:** replacing `{action:"x", ...input}` with a `payload` parameter breaks typecheck — the old spread produced a fresh object literal, so optional (`input?`) and interface-typed args were assignable. Use `payload: object | undefined`, not `Record<string, unknown>`. `make pre-pr` caught it; the background-task exit code was reported 0 while `make` actually exited 2 — **read the pre-pr output, don't trust the notification's exit code**.

**Guards added (both mutation-tested):**
- `__tests__/unit/http/rest-fixed-action-args.test.ts` — pure `fixedActionArgs` precedence + a source guard over `index.ts` asserting exactly ONE bare `restToolProxy(` remains (the generic `POST /api/:orgSlug/:toolName` passthrough).
- `__tests__/unit/sandbox/action-discriminator-source.test.ts` — no file in `sandbox/namespaces/` may match `(payload|input|args|rest).action`, plus a non-vacuity assertion that it found >5 files.

Put `fixedActionArgs` in `src/http/rest-tool-action.ts`, NOT in `rest-api.ts` — importing `rest-api` pulls the whole tool graph and the unit test dies on `Cannot find module '@lobu/connector-sdk'`.

Related: [[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]] (the sandbox instance came from grep-enumerating the class, not a second review round), [[feedback_guards_must_assert_coverage]], [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].

**PR #2360** is open: https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2360 — `make review` running now (once, on settled HEAD).

## What shipped to the PR

One root cause, three instances — caller input overriding a discriminator the server had fixed:

| where | shape | reachable via |
|---|---|---|
| REST wrappers | `{ action: "list", ...c.req.query() }` | cross-site link (`SameSite=Lax` GET) |
| sandbox `action` | `action(payload.action as string, …)` | read-mode `query_sdk` script |
| sandbox `schema_type` | `{ schema_type: "entity_type", ...payload }` | same |

Not privilege escalation in any of them — `executeTool` re-checks access level on both paths. What each does is let an already-authorized principal be steered into a write they didn't ask for. Sharpest case stays `GET /api/{org}/runs?action=approve&run_id=N`: member-tier, and it supplies the human decision the approval gate exists to require.

Fixed at the chokepoint rather than per-site: `restToolAction` applies the action last, and sandbox discriminators are literals from the call site.

## Confidence

- **REST fix — high (90).** Red→green on the real composition, chokepoint verified by a guard asserting exactly one bare `restToolProxy(` remains, and that guard mutation-tested.
- **Sandbox fix — high (88).** review-fix's behavioural test is red against the actual pre-fix file from `HEAD` and green after; covers both discriminators.
- **Not exercised against a booted server (60).** Everything above is unit-level plus `make pre-pr`. I did not boot the app and issue a real `GET …?action=delete` against a live org — so the end-to-end claim rests on argument-composition tests, not an observed non-deletion. Worth saying plainly.
- **Prod exposure severity — high (92).** Probed directly against prod, anonymously.

## Suggested next

1. **Let CI + `pi-review` report, then merge** — I won't `--admin` past an unreported check, and I'd rather you eyeball the diff first.
2. **The `connect_token` PR** — separate branch, not started. 49 fields served anonymously on public orgs; `connect_token` is wired into the shape and currently null only because no flow is pending.
3. **Decide the consolidation abstraction** — still the open question that decides whether it's a contained change or a capability vocabulary across both doors. The revised design constraints are now in memory, so it survives this session either way.
4. **Two prod-verifies still owed** from earlier work (#2358 rolled out, #2315) — unrelated to this PR but sitting in the open-work list.
what's sandbox schema type etc i don't undestand

Fair — I compressed three things into a phrase. Concretely:

**The sandbox** is the ClientSDK that agent scripts run in — `query_sdk` / `run_sdk`. An agent writes `client.entitySchema.listTypes(...)` and that gets translated into a tool call.

**`schema_type`** is a field on the `manageEntitySchema` tool. That one tool handles two different kinds of thing:
- `schema_type: "entity_type"` → the entity types themselves (`company`, `person`, `goal`)
- `schema_type: "relationship_type"` → the links between them (`works_at`)

And `action` says what to do (`list`, `create`, `delete`). So the tool needs **two** fields to know what it's being asked — that's what I meant by "doubly discriminated". `listTypes()` is supposed to mean "`action: list` + `schema_type: entity_type`", both fixed by the SDK, not by the agent.

**The bug.** Both fixed values were written *before* the caller's input was spread in, so the input overwrote them:

```ts
listTypes: (input) => callEntity({ action: "list", ...input }, "listTypes")
//                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^^^^^ input wins

callEntity = (payload) => action(
  payload.action as string,                    // ← read back off the payload
  { schema_type: "entity_type", ...payload },  // ← input wins again
)
```

So an agent calling:

```js
client.entitySchema.listTypes({ action: "delete", schema_type: "relationship_type", slug: "works_at" })
```

got `action = "delete"` and `schema_type = "relationship_type"` — it deleted a relationship type, through a method named `listTypes`.

**After** — both pinned, and the action is a literal that's never read back off the payload:

```ts
listTypes: (input) => callEntity("list", input, "listTypes")

callEntity = (actionName, payload) => action(
  actionName,
  { ...payload, schema_type: "entity_type" },  // ← fixed value last
)
```

**Why it mattered.** `query_sdk` has a read-only mode: it filters the SDK manifest so only read-tier methods exist — `deleteType` isn't offered, `listTypes` is. This let a script reach the delete handler through the method that *was* offered, so read-mode wasn't actually read-only.

**Why it isn't a breach.** `executeTool` independently re-checks the caller's access level, so the script only got what its credentials already allowed. A read-tier agent got refused. The failure is narrower: an admin-credentialed agent running deliberately in read mode could still mutate — which defeats the point of read mode, but doesn't hand anyone permissions they didn't have.

I found the `action` half by grepping the class after the REST fix; `make review-fix` caught the `schema_type` half, which I'd missed.

Checked properly. Short answer: **yes, compatible, and there's no duplication** — with one caveat about what "compatible" means.

## Not duplicated — one implementation, two entry points

```ts
runSdkScript   = withValidatedArgs("run_sdk",   RunSchema,   (a,e,c) => runSandbox("full", a, e, c))
querySdkScript = withValidatedArgs("query_sdk", QuerySchema, (a,e,c) => runSandbox("read", a, e, c))
```

Same `runSandbox`, same sandbox, same dispatch. The tools differ by a single string. Schemas share `SCRIPT_FIELDS`; `RunSchema` is `{...SCRIPT_FIELDS, dry_run}` and `QuerySchema` is `SCRIPT_FIELDS` verbatim. So `dry_run` is the only field that exists in one and not the other — correctly, since there's nothing to preview in read mode.

## No gaps — exact 1:1, both directions

```
RUNTIME methods: 127 | METADATA entries: 127
by access tier: {"read":46, "write":23, "admin":48, "external":10}
```

Not just equal counts — `method-metadata.test.ts` already enforces both directions: every runtime method has metadata (nothing silently unreachable), and every metadata entry has a runtime method (no phantom docs `search_sdk` advertises but the sandbox rejects — the comment cites retired `behaviors.upgrade` as the case that motivated it).

## run_sdk is a strict superset of query_sdk, at every caller tier

```
caller=read:  query_sdk=46  run_sdk=46   | in query_sdk but NOT run_sdk: []
caller=write: query_sdk=46  run_sdk=79   | in query_sdk but NOT run_sdk: []
caller=admin: query_sdk=46  run_sdk=127  | in query_sdk but NOT run_sdk: []
```

Nothing is reachable through `query_sdk` that isn't also reachable through `run_sdk`. So any read script ports to `run_sdk` unchanged — that's the compatibility you were asking about.

## The caveat worth knowing

`query_sdk` shows **46 methods regardless of who you are** — an admin gets exactly the same surface as a read-tier caller. That's deliberate (`sdkMethodVisible`: `if (mode === "read") return methodAccess === "read"`), and it's the whole point of read mode: the tool, not the credential, bounds what you can do.

Which is exactly what the bug in this PR was breaking. `entitySchema.listTypes({action:'delete'})` was the one hole in that model — a way to reach a write handler through one of the 46. So the answer to "is the split clean?" is: the model was already sound and well-guarded, and the PR closes the one place it leaked.

One thing I did *not* verify: whether all 46 read-tier classifications are correct — i.e. that no method labelled `read` in `METHOD_METADATA` actually writes. The tests prove every method *has* a label, not that the label is *true*. That's an audit of 46 handlers, and it's the natural follow-up if you want the read-mode guarantee fully nailed down.

**Merged.** PR #2360 → squash `0b641f5c`. All 9 required checks green including `integration`; local suites 745 + 64 pass, 0 fail. Worktree and branch cleaned, no stray files. Prod rollout gate is running in the background.

## No — we did not consolidate. Be clear on this.

You asked me to do the public-workspace consolidation. **That is not built.** What shipped is a security fix I found *while investigating* it. Where each piece actually stands:

| | status |
|---|---|
| Action-discriminator fix (3 instances) | ✅ merged `0b641f5c` |
| Public-workspace REST/tool consolidation — **the original task** | ❌ not started; design needs rework |
| `connect_token` / `created_by` anonymous exposure | ❌ not started |
| Org-root product decision for non-members | ❌ blocked on you |

The consolidation didn't get built because the codex review falsified the design's premises, and I'm not going to implement a design I know is wrong:

- `/public/*` is **not** redundant — I'd checked one handler and generalized to seven. Deleting it would have broken public workspace browsing and dropped `/public/connectors/:key` and `/public/organization`, which have no equivalent.
- `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` gates **action names, not fields**. Declaring `GET /connections` ≡ `manage_connections.list` would have inherited all 49 fields including `connect_token`. The declaration has to gate the projection, which is a materially bigger change than "teach REST the policy".

So the honest read: this session converted a wrong plan into a correct, merged fix plus a corrected design — but the consolidation itself is still open, and it's now a larger piece of work than the handoff doc implied, not a smaller one.

## Two things still blocked on you

1. **The abstraction** — projection-level capabilities everywhere (codex's recommendation, touches both doors), or `(tool, action)` coupling only for routes that literally proxy a fixed action with explicit DTOs for agents and `/installed`. This decides the size of the work.
2. **What a non-member sees at a public workspace root.** No policy change fixes it; the builder is genuinely owner-only.

## One thing I'd flag unprompted

`git worktree list` shows **46 worktrees**, many on branches that look long-merged. I only cleaned my own — I'm not deleting others' without you saying so, since some may be live work. Worth a sweep sometime, classified by `gh pr` state rather than ancestry (squash merges make ancestry lie, which is exactly why `task-clean` refused mine).

Also unverified, and the natural follow-up to your `query_sdk` question: the 46 `read`-tier labels are proven to *exist*, not proven to be *true*. If a handler labelled `read` actually writes, read-mode leaks — same shape as the bug just fixed, one layer up.

/**
 * What a caller with no org membership may see on a connection.
 *
 * `manage_connections.list` / `.get` are in PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS, so on a
 * PUBLIC org they answer anonymous callers. Both handlers select `c.*` plus
 * joined auth-profile / device columns and a live `connect_token` subselect,
 * then spread the row into the response — 49 fields, verified anonymously
 * against a prod public org. That set includes a pending `connect_token`
 * (a one-hour bearer capability that resolves the connection and starts
 * OAuth), the creator's user id and username, auth-profile identifiers, and
 * device labels/handles/last-seen.
 *
 * This is an ALLOW-list, not a deny-list, and that is the point: a column
 * added to `connections` later is hidden from anonymous readers by default
 * instead of leaking until someone remembers to exclude it. Members are
 * unaffected — the console reads the full row.
 */

import type { ToolContext } from "../../registry";

/**
 * Connection fields safe for a non-member reader: what the connection IS and
 * how much of it there is. Nothing about credentials, the humans behind it,
 * the device running it, or its internal wiring.
 */
export const PUBLIC_CONNECTION_FIELDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
	// identity of the connection itself
	"id",
	"slug",
	"display_name",
	"connector_key",
	"connector_name",
	"status",
	"visibility",
	"created_at",
	"updated_at",
	// shape / volume — what the public connectors listing renders
	"feed_count",
	"data_feed_count",
	"entity_ids",
	"entity_names",
	"declares_chat",
	"has_feeds_schema",
	"has_operations",
	"operations_summary",
	"facets",
]);

/**
 * Narrow one connection row to the public field set when the caller is not a
 * member of the org.
 *
 * Gated on `memberRole` rather than `isAuthenticated`: an authenticated
 * non-member on a public org is admitted with `memberRole: null`
 * (workspace/multi-tenant.ts), and is exactly as unentitled to a connect
 * token as an anonymous one. System/internal contexts also carry no
 * memberRole and are narrowed too — `connect` mints and returns its own
 * token on the admin-gated path, so no legitimate caller depends on
 * list/get to hand one back.
 */
export function projectConnectionForReader(
	row: Record<string, unknown>,
	ctx: ToolContext
): Record<string, unknown> {
	if (ctx.memberRole) return row;

	const projected: Record<string, unknown> = {};
	for (const key of Object.keys(row)) {
		if (PUBLIC_CONNECTION_FIELDS.has(key)) projected[key] = row[key];
	}
	return projected;
}

## #2360 is live in prod — but I have to walk back part of my verification

The rollout gate opened: deployed revision is `0b641f5c`, the squash commit. So the code is out.

My prod check, though, **did not verify the fix**:

```
GET /connections?action=delete&connection_id=1  -> 401
GET /runs?action=approve&run_id=1               -> 401
```

Anonymous callers were *always* 401 on those routes — `mcpAuth` blocked them before and after. I checked the path that was never vulnerable. The vulnerable caller was an **authenticated member or admin**, whose cookie rides along on a cross-site GET. So those 401s tell us nothing about whether the fix works in prod.

A real verification would authenticate as a member and issue `GET /connections?action=delete&connection_id=<nonexistent>`. That's safely non-destructive against an id that doesn't exist, and it discriminates cleanly: fixed → action forced to `list`, returns 200 with an array; broken → `delete` on a missing row, returns a not-found error. I haven't run it because it needs a real prod credential, and I'm not going to go looking for one of your tokens to fire authenticated write-shaped requests at production without you saying so.

So: **merged and deployed, unit-verified, prod-unverified.** The honest confidence is high on the code (red→green, guards mutation-tested, 0 review blockers) and *unmeasured* on prod behaviour.

## Meanwhile, PR 2 (`connect_token`)

Hit the same misleading-exit-code trap — `make pre-pr` reported exit 0 while actually failing with `TS2339: Property 'connection' does not exist`. My cast to `ManageConnectionsResult["connection"]` was wrong because the result is a union. Turned out the contract types it as `Record<string, unknown>`, which is exactly what the projection returns — so both casts came out entirely. Typecheck now exit 0 (checked explicitly, not through a pipe), 752 unit tests pass, full pre-pr re-running.

That's twice this session the notification said 0 while `make` exited 2. I've written it to memory; worth knowing it's not reliable.

## Two things I want to flag rather than bury

**The prod-verify gap is systemic, not specific to this PR.** Memory lists prod-verify OWED against several merged programs. The pattern is that verifying an authenticated-only fix needs a credential, so it silently never happens. If you want these actually closed, the unblock is a long-lived test PAT on a throwaway org — otherwise "prod-verify owed" will keep accumulating.

**Still blocked on your three answers**, and I'd rather stop than guess: the consolidation abstraction, the public-workspace root, and whether to audit the 46 read-tier labels. The `connect_token` PR is the last thing I can finish without them.

## Summary

- `manage_connections.list` / `.get` are in `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`, so on a **public** org they answer anonymous callers. Both select `c.*` plus joined auth-profile/device columns and a live `connect_token` subselect, then spread the row into the response.
- Verified anonymously against prod (`market.lobu.ai`, public org, no credentials): **49 fields**, including `connect_token` — a one-hour bearer capability that resolves the connection and starts OAuth — plus `created_by` (raw user id) and `created_by_username`.
- Non-member readers are now narrowed to an explicit **allow-list** of 18 fields. Members are unaffected: the console reads the full row.

**Nothing is currently leaking a credential.** There are 0 pending `connect_tokens` org-wide, so the field comes back `null` today. What shipped here is closing the shape before one exists: any connect flow started on an org-visible connection in a public org would have exposed a live token to unauthenticated callers for its lifetime. `created_by` / `created_by_username`, by contrast, *were* being served (11 connections in one public org).

### Why an allow-list, not a deny-list

The handlers are `SELECT c.*`. A deny-list leaks every column added to `connections` later, until someone remembers to exclude it. The allow-list fails closed — there's a test asserting an unknown future column is withheld.

### Why `memberRole`, not `isAuthenticated`

A public org admits a **signed-in non-member** with `memberRole: null` (`workspace/multi-tenant.ts`). They are exactly as unentitled to a connect token as an anonymous caller. Covered by its own test.

## Test plan

- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (verified via explicit `make exit=0`, not the reported task exit code — it has been wrong twice this session)
- [x] Tests run: `bun test packages/server/src/__tests__/unit` — 752 pass / 0 fail
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: n/a

### Red (projection disabled → pre-fix passthrough)

```
(fail) withholds every sensitive field from an anonymous reader
(fail) withholds a live connect token specifically
(fail) withholds it from an authenticated NON-member too
(fail) is an allow-list, so an unknown future column is withheld by default
 3 pass, 4 fail
```

### Green

```
 7 pass, 0 fail, 50 expect() calls
```

## No SPA consumer breaks

Checked the call sites rather than inferring: the console already branches on `canManageWorkspace` and routes non-members to `/api/{org}/public/connectors` instead of `manage_connections.list` (`owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/events-tab/index.tsx:238-260`). Every SPA path that reaches `manage_connections.list` is member-gated.

Visible effect for a non-member on a public workspace's connector detail page: connection cards render fewer badges (no auth-profile status, no device label). That is the intent.

## Scope — this is instance 1 of a class, deliberately

The same shape (public-readable tool spreading a raw row) exists in at least `manage_operations.list_runs` (returns run input/output/checkpoints), `manage_feeds`, `manage_classifiers`, and `manage_catalog.list_installed` (`source_uri` can be a server-local `file://` path).

AGENTS.md says fix the class in the branch that finds it. Not done here, on purpose: fixing all of them *is* the pending "projection-level capabilities" design decision (see the codex design review on the public-workspace transport gap). Committing to it through an unreviewed branch would decide that architecture by the back door. This PR fixes the instance that contains a live credential; the rest are named as follow-up.

If the capability design lands, `PUBLIC_CONNECTION_FIELDS` becomes the first capability's field allow-list rather than a one-off.

## Notes

Related: #2360 (action-discriminator override) came out of the same investigation. Both are consequences of `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` gating **action names, not fields** — the finding that sent the original consolidation design back for revision.

**#2360** — action-discriminator override (3 instances). Merged `0b641f5c`, rolled out to prod, all gates green, 0 review blockers. Prod-*verified* only for the anonymous path, which was never the vulnerable one — the authenticated-caller check needs a credential I haven't asked you for.

## Two judgment calls in that PR worth your eye

**Allow-list over deny-list.** The handlers are `SELECT c.*`, so a deny-list leaks any column added later. There's a test asserting an unknown future column is withheld. Costs: 18 fields pass, 31 don't — if the public UI later needs one, it's an additive change plus a test, not a silent fix.

AGENTS.md says fix the class in the branch that finds it, and I'm knowingly not doing that — because fixing all of them *is* the projection-capabilities decision from question 1. Doing it here would settle that architecture on a branch you haven't reviewed. I'd rather break the rule visibly and say so than commit you sideways.

## Where it stops

After this PR I'm out of work that doesn't require a decision from you:

- **Consolidation abstraction** — proxy-only coupling vs projection capabilities. Determines whether the above is 1 PR or 5, and whether the *tool* door narrows too (a live behaviour change).
- **Public workspace root** — pure product call; no reading of the code decides it.
- **The 46 read-tier labels** — proven to exist, not proven true. A handler labelled `read` that writes would leak through `query_sdk` read-mode, same shape as what just merged, one layer up.

The design constraints are all written to memory, so none of this is lost if you come back to it later.

input.new_string:
### Why `memberRole`, not `isAuthenticated`

A public org admits a **signed-in non-member** with `memberRole: null` (`workspace/multi-tenant.ts`). They are exactly as unentitled to a connect token as an anonymous caller. Covered by its own test.

### The system-caller carve-out needs `tokenType`, not bare `isSystemContext`

In-process system calls (watcher reactions) keep the full row — they read `credential_mode` / `error_message` / device fields to decide what to do, and narrowing them would break reactions silently rather than loudly.

But `isSystemContext` alone is **not** a safe data-exposure boundary. It was written to bypass role/scope policy at the handler boundary, and its shape (`isAuthenticated && !userId && !memberRole`) is equally satisfied by a **token minted without a user** — `multi-tenant.ts` builds token auth as `userId: tokenData.userId || undefined`, and `AuthInfo.userId` is `string | null | undefined`. Such a token, non-member, on a public org over MCP would have read as "system" and collected a live `connect_token`.

The carve-out therefore also requires `tokenType === 'session'`, which excludes every token caller (`pat` / `access_token` / `Bearer`) and anonymous. A real browser session carries `session` too but has a `userId`, so `isSystemContext` already excludes it.

This gap was introduced by the `review-fix` pass and caught by verifying its diff. Test `does not treat a userId-less TOKEN as a system caller` is red against the bare-`isSystemContext` version:

```
(fail) does not treat a userId-less TOKEN as a system caller
 6 pass, 1 fail
```

content.text:
**PR #2363** open: https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2363 — `make review` running.

## Two catches worth reporting, both from verifying rather than trusting

**review-fix introduced a security gap, and I caught it.** It replaced my `memberRole`-only gate with `isSystemContext(ctx)`. That concept exists in the codebase and fixing my version was *right* in intent — I'd have broken watcher reactions, which read `credential_mode`/`error_message`/device fields and would have silently received 18 fields.

But `isSystemContext` is `isAuthenticated && !userId && !memberRole`, and `multi-tenant.ts` builds token auth as `userId: tokenData.userId || undefined` with `AuthInfo.userId` typed `string | null | undefined`. So a **token minted without a user** satisfies it — and on a public org over MCP would have been handed the full row including a live `connect_token`. The carve-out now also requires `tokenType === 'session'`. Proven with a test that's red against review-fix's version:

```
(fail) does not treat a userId-less TOKEN as a system caller     6 pass, 1 fail
```

`isSystemContext` was written to bypass *role/scope policy at the handler boundary*. Reusing it as a *data-exposure* boundary is where it stopped holding.

**review-fix also wrote an integration test I nearly failed to ship.** `gh pr create` warned "1 uncommitted change" — I'd staged by explicit path and missed it. It's better than my unit test: it inserts a real pending `connect_token` and asserts the **owner still receives it**, which makes the non-member assertions non-vacuous — they're withholding something, not observing an empty column. Committed as a second commit.

Had I not read that warning, the PR would have shipped without its strongest test.

| #2360 action-discriminator | merged `0b641f5c`, **live in prod** |
| #2363 connection projection | open, gates green, review running |

Local: 752 unit pass / 0 fail, `make pre-pr` clean (`make exit=0`, checked explicitly — it misreported twice today). Integration test will be verified by CI's required `integration` check; I haven't run it locally, no `DATABASE_URL` here.

## Still yours, still unanswered

The consolidation abstraction, the public workspace root, and the 46 read-tier label audit. I'm now genuinely out of work that doesn't depend on one of them — both PRs came from the *investigation*, not the task you set. The consolidation itself remains unbuilt, and I'd be guessing at architecture to start it.

Waiting on `integration` — I'll merge when it reports, and not before (it's the only gate that runs the new integration test).

## Session summary

**Merged and live:** #2360 — action-discriminator override, three instances of one root cause. Prod rollout confirmed at `0b641f5c`.

**Ready to merge:** #2363 — connection credential/identity projection. 8/9 required checks green, `pi-review` 88 with 0 blockers, `integration` pending.

## What actually happened versus what you asked for

You asked for the public-workspace consolidation. **It is not built.** Both PRs came out of investigating it, not doing it. The design review falsified three of my premises — `/public/*` isn't redundant, four of seven routes already gate at `executeTool`, and `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` bounds action names rather than fields — and the last of those is what turned a "teach REST the policy" change into a projection-design problem I won't guess at.

The corrected design constraints are in memory, so the work survives this session either way.

## The pattern worth taking away

Three times today the thing that caught a real defect was reading output rather than trusting a signal:

- `make pre-pr` reported exit 0 while `make` exited 2 — twice. Both were real typecheck failures.
- `make review-fix` fixed a bug I'd introduced *and* introduced one of its own (`isSystemContext` as a data-exposure boundary, satisfiable by a userId-less token).
- `gh pr create` warned "1 uncommitted change" — that was the strongest test in the PR, nearly unshipped.

Automated passes are useful and were right more often than not. They aren't evidence on their own.

## Open, and genuinely blocked on you

1. **Consolidation abstraction** — proxy-only coupling vs projection capabilities. Decides 1 PR or 5, and whether the tool door narrows (a live behaviour change).
2. **Public workspace root** — product call; the builder is owner-only and no policy change alters that.
3. **The 46 read-tier labels** — proven to exist, not proven true. Same shape as what merged today, one layer up.

Plus a systemic one: verifying an authenticated-only fix in prod needs a credential, which is why "prod-verify owed" keeps accumulating in memory across several programs. A long-lived test PAT on a throwaway org would unblock the whole class.

import { isSystemContext } from "../../access-control";

const PUBLIC_CONNECTION_FIELDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([

Found 2026-07-30 on `legal-review.lobu.ai` (org `legal-review`, visibility `public`). Handoff doc written to `/tmp/public-workspace-rest-transport-gap.md`. UNFIXED.

**The carve-out only sees tool calls.** `canAccessPublicOrgRequest()` (`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:180`) bails on `!requestedToolName` and on any non-POST/PUT/PATCH method, so a `GET /api/{org}/...` REST route can *never* be public-readable. It never reaches its handler — the middleware answers 401 (`:610`, anonymous) or 403 (`:566`, authenticated non-member).

**The bug: same data, two doors, opposite answers.** `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` at `packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:181` already declares `manage_agents: new Set(["list","get"])` public. Live, anonymous:
- `POST /api/legal-review/manage_agents {"action":"list"}` → **200**
- `GET  /api/legal-review/agents` → **401**

A transport gap, NOT a policy gap. The policy is written; the REST door doesn't consult it.

**Why some public pages work:** Activity uses `resolve_path` + `manage_operations.list_activity`; Connectors uses `manage_connections.list` / `manage_catalog.list_catalog` + `/api/{org}/public/*`. All tool-transport or the explicit public REST namespace → they render. The org root and the agents list use plain REST → they 401.

## Corrections from the 2026-07-30 design review (codex + prod probes) — the original handoff doc was wrong on three points

1. **`legal-review` has 0 agent rows.** Its empty sidebar is truthful data, NOT the 401. Do not use it as the witness. Use **`atlas`** (public, 2 agents incl. a system agent): there `manage_agents.list` returns both agents anonymously while `GET /api/atlas/agents` is 401. Public orgs w/ agents: atlas 2, devops/market/delivery 1 each.
2. **`/api/{org}/public/*` is NOT redundant** — do not plan to delete it. Only `behaviors` is a thin wrapper. `/public/knowledge/search` accepts MORE params than its authed sibling (`rest-api.ts:442` vs `:395`); `/public/connectors/:key` is a unique composite projection with no equivalent; `/public/organization` has no public-readable tool at all; `/public/events` applies a strict invalidation-key filter `/events` lacks. Checking one handler and generalizing to the namespace was the error.
3. **"REST has no execution-time gate" is false for 4 of 7 routes.** `connections`, `runs`, `actions/available` go through `restToolProxy` → `executeTool` → `isPublicReadable` (`tools/execute.ts:184`). Only the two agent routes and `/installed` lack it.

**The finding that reshapes the design:** `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` is an *action-name* allow-list and says nothing about FIELDS. `manage_connections.list` is `SELECT c.*` (`crud.ts:270`) + a live `connect_token` subselect (`:305`). Verified anonymous on prod `market.lobu.ai`: **49 fields**, incl. `created_by`, `created_by_username`, and `connect_token` (null only because 0 tokens pending). `list_runs` returns run input/output/checkpoints; `/installed` leaks `source_uri` (can be a server-local `file://`). So "declare REST route ≡ tool action" would inherit every field — the declaration must gate the PROJECTION, not just the route.

**Design verdict:** implement projection-level capabilities with one canonical serializer per capability, or keep `(tool, action)` coupling ONLY for routes that literally proxy a fixed tool action (connections/runs/actions — which already gate at `executeTool`), and give agents + `/installed` explicit public DTOs.

**Hono seam (empirically resolved):** `c.req.routePath` returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents/*` before `next()` — useless for distinguishing list from detail. Use Hono's `routePath(c, -1)` helper, which returns `/api/:orgSlug/agents` and `/api/:orgSlug/agents/:agentId` correctly; `baseRoutePath(c, -1)` gives the mount prefix. Registry miss must deny.

**Separately, the org root is a product problem, not a policy one.** `packages/owletto/src/app/$owner.tsx:42` calls `useSystemAgentId()` unconditionally and `:110-117` renders `systemAgentError.message` verbatim. No policy change fixes it — the builder is genuinely owner-only (`set_system_agent` is in OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS). The root must stop requesting it for non-members. Reuse what exists: `useCurrentOrg()` → `{isMember,isPublic}`, `PublicOrgJoinBar` (already mounted in the shell), and the SSR-injected `__LOBU_PUBLIC_BOOTSTRAP__.resolvedPath.workspace`.

**Three viewer states at the org root** — only the first is fixed (by #2358):
| anonymous + private | ✅ redirect to sign-in |
| authenticated non-member + private | ❌ raw 403 |
| any non-member + public | ❌ this gap |

Preserve the deliberate carve-out: a 5xx outage must keep rendering the error, never bounce to sign-in.

Related: [[project_org_root_signin_guard]], [[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]].

## Summary

A public organization's REST door refused GETs that its tool door already answered anonymously. `canAccessPublicOrgRequest` (`workspace/multi-tenant.ts`) could only ever see a tool name on a JSON POST body — a `GET /api/{org}/runs` carried none, so it was denied before reaching a handler.

Verified anonymously against prod (`market.lobu.ai`, public org, no credentials):

| data | tool door | REST door |
|---|---|---|
| connections list | `POST manage_connections {"action":"list"}` → **200** | `GET /connections` → **401** |
| runs | `POST manage_operations {"action":"list_runs"}` → **200** | `GET /runs` → **401** |
| available actions | `POST manage_operations {"action":"list_available"}` → **200** | `GET /actions/available` → **401** |

Same data, two doors, opposite answers. A transport gap, not a policy gap — the policy was already written in `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`; the REST door just couldn't consult it.

## What changed

One declaration table (`http/rest-tool-routes.ts`) names the fixed `(tool, action)` for the four GET routes that are *pure* proxies. Two consumers read it:

- `index.ts` **registers the routes from it**, so the pair the middleware authorizes is the pair the handler executes — they cannot drift.
- `multi-tenant.ts` resolves a live request to its declaration and asks the existing `isPublicReadable`.

**This widens the transport, never the policy.** Every declared pair is one the tool door already served anonymously; a unit test asserts that, so a future entry that is *not* public-readable fails the build. `executeTool`'s own `isPublicReadable` check still runs — this doesn't remove a gate, it adds one earlier.

## Scope — agents and `/installed` stay closed, deliberately

`manage_agents.list` and `manage_catalog.list_installed` are both public-readable, and both REST routes are also 401 today. They are **not** declared here: their handlers are hand-rolled and return a superset of the tool payload (the agents route adds connection/watcher/user counts, platforms, providers). Declaring them would claim a public-readability their responses do not honour — the same field-vs-action confusion behind #2360 and #2363.

They need an explicit public projection first, the shape `manage_connections/public-projection.ts` established in #2363. An integration test pins `/agents` at 401 so this stays a decision rather than a drift.

Related finding, not fixed here: `manage_agents.list` already returns `owner_user_id` (a raw user id) anonymously on a public org — same class as the `created_by` exposure fixed in #2363.

---
name: reference_hono_routepath_catchall_trap
description: In Hono middleware use routePath(c), NOT routePath(c,-1) — the SPA catch-all makes the "last matched route" resolve to /*, silently disabling route-pattern lookups in prod while tests pass.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Resolving "which route pattern am I on?" from inside Hono middleware:

- **`routePath(c)`** — the currently-executing route. **Correct.**
- **`routePath(c, -1)`** — the LAST matched route. **Wrong in this repo.**
- `c.req.routePath` — mount pattern before `next()` (`/api/:orgSlug/agents/*`); cannot tell list from detail. Also wrong.

`packages/server/src/index.ts:2785` mounts a SPA catch-all `app.get("*", …)`. Every API GET therefore matches its own route AND the catch-all, and `matchedRoutes(c)` *ends on the catch-all*, so `routePath(c, -1)` returns `/*`:

```
/api/market/connections  routePath(c)= /api/:orgSlug/connections  routePath(c,-1)= /*
/api/market/runs         routePath(c)= /api/:orgSlug/runs         routePath(c,-1)= /*
POST .../manage_connections  both = /api/:orgSlug/:toolName   <- POST has no catch-all, so it agrees
```

Note the POST case agrees — which is exactly why a partial test looks fine.

**This corrects an earlier note in [[project_public_workspace_rest_transport_gap]] that said to use `routePath(c, -1)`.** That was measured on a test app registering only API routes. With no catch-all present the two helpers agree; add the catch-all and they diverge for GET only. A pattern-lookup keyed on `routePath(c, -1)` misses, denies, and the feature is a **silent no-op in production while its own tests pass green**. Caught on PR #2364 by `make review-fix`, not by my tests.

**Rule: a Hono routing test must reproduce the production route table** — global `/*` middleware AND the trailing `app.get("*")` — or it is not testing routing. Shipped in #2364 with a mutation test (`routePath(c)` → `routePath(c, -1)`) that fails both the unit and integration suites.

Related: [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]], [[feedback_verify_the_surface_not_the_builder]].
